title: Incident scripting and stakeholder briefs: responder patterns, templates, and game-day scripts
author: Daniela Ruiz
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document provides canonical incident "scripting" — short, repeatable sequences for responders to follow during common incident classes — and stakeholder brief templates used for status pages, customer notices, and internal escalation. It is intended for oncall engineers, SRE responders, support, and product incident leads.

Scope: covers classification and initial triage, responder roles and play scripts for three priority incident classes (latency spike, model quality regression, capacity exhaustion), status page and customer notice templates, handoff checklists, and a game-day syllabus to validate scripts.

Guiding principles
- Keep early communications precise, time-bounded, and action-oriented.
- Use templated language to avoid confusion and legal exposure.
- Work in 15-minute cycles for high-severity incidents: detect -> assess -> mitigate -> communicate.
- Prefer graceful degradation (fallback models, reduced throughput) over hard failovers where possible.

Incident classification and thresholds
- P0 (Sev1): Global or multi-region outage affecting >25% of active requests or an SLO breach >5% sustained for 5m.
- P1 (Sev2): Significant latency or error spike affecting a major route (>10% requests) or single-customer degrading impact.
- P2 (Sev3): Isolated errors, degraded accuracy for small prompt sets, or minor infra alerts.

SLOs and detection signals (examples)
- Token latency p99: 500ms target; alert at p99 > 800ms for 5m.
- Request error rate: alert when 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 5m.
- Model-quality regression (production eval set): A/B delta with control >3% for two consecutive evaluation runs.

Responder roles and contact matrix
- Incident Lead (IL): coordinates the overall response, runs bridge, owns external comms. Primary: oncall-eng; Escalation: Eng SRE Lead.
- Mitigation Engineer (ME): implements technical mitigations (scaling, rollback, cache flush).
- Model Owner (MO): responsible for model-level rollbacks, quality mitigations.
- Communications Lead (CL): drafts and posts status page updates and customer notices.
- Support Liaison (SL): summarizes customer-facing impact and routes tickets to IL.

Contact table (text)
- IL: #oncall-bridge (pager) -> oncall rotation -> eng-sre@redwood.com
- ME: runtime-team rotation -> slack @runtime-oncall
- MO: model-onboarding team -> slack @model-owner-oncall
- CL: comms rotation -> slack @ops-comms

Play scripts (short, repeatable sequences)
1) Latency spike (Sev2 -> potential Sev1)
- Trigger: p99 latency exceeds alert threshold or regional p95 degrades by 2x.
- 0–5m (Assess): Incident Lead opens bridge, posts initial note: "Investigating increased token latency in <region>. Initial triage underway. Updates every 15 minutes." Assign Mitigation Engineer and check autoscaling events, queue lengths, GPU saturation.
- 5–15m (Mitigate): If autoscaling lag: temporarily increase replica weight or add burst instances for affected group. If one model variant shows heavy tail: route traffic to alternative compatible model (see routing policy).
- 15–30m (Stabilize): Validate p99 return to within 20% of baseline. If not, prepare rollback to prior model version or reduce concurrency. CL posts customer-facing status: see template A.
- Post-incident: IL runs short postmortem using template in "Postmortem skeleton" section.

2) Model quality regression (Sev2)
- Trigger: production eval detects regression or customers report consistent incorrect outputs.
- 0–5m (Assess): MO pulls latest diffs, checks rollout logs, and inspects prompting changes. Open bridge and tag product and support.
- 5–20m (Mitigate): If recent model rollout: immediately pin traffic to previous model version and suspend the current rollout. If model drift due to prompt ecosystem: enable prompt sanitizer or apply guardrail reranking.
- 20–60m (Correct): Run a targeted evaluation on the failing prompt set and triage whether quantization/profile change caused regression. If code/config related, revert commit. CL issues customer guidance: see template B.
- Post-incident: MO publishes a model root-cause note and follow-up quality tests to our eval harness.

3) Capacity exhaustion (Sev1 if sustained)
- Trigger: GPU pool saturation, autoscaler unable to provision within SLA windows, or complete region capacity loss.
- 0–3m (Immediate containment): IL enables degraded routing: shift non-critical traffic to backup region, enable rate-limit backpressure for lower-tier plans using token-bucket policies. Post initial public notice.
- 3–30m (Recovery): ME requests burst capacity via Dedicated pool or triggers reserved burst in config. If capacity cannot be procured, enforce firm throttles per plan until capacity returns.
- Post-incident: Full capacity review and committed capacity procurement policy update.

Runbook snippets (commands and checks)
- Check p99 latency: curl -s "https://metrics-api.internal/api/queries/p99?service=runtime&window=5m" | jq .value
- Inspect GPU utilization: kubectl top pods -l app=runtime --namespace=prod | sort -k3 -r
- Trigger rollback (example CLI): rwctl rollout rollback --service runtime --model-id rdm-20250115-v2 --reason "quality_regression"

Status page and customer notice templates
Template A (Initial short public status)
- Title: Service degradation - increased response latency (region)
- Time: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Summary: We are investigating increased response times for API requests in <region>. Some customers may experience slower responses or timeouts.
- Impact: Intermittent latency increases and request timeouts affecting <X>% of requests.
- Mitigation in progress: Diverting traffic and scaling additional capacity; engineers are actively investigating root cause.
- Next update: in 15 minutes or sooner.

Template B (Customer-facing follow-up with guidance)
- Subject: Update: Ongoing quality regression impacting responses for <model-name>
- Greeting: Hello,
- Body: We've identified an issue affecting output quality for requests routed to <model-name> starting at <time>. We have rolled back to the previous stable version while the team completes a thorough root cause analysis. If you rely on specific prompt patterns, please reach out to support with examples so we can prioritize remediation.
- ETA: Estimated resolution time: <window> or "under investigation".
- Contacts: support@redwood.com (for account-specific impact).

Template C (Detailed customer post-incident report)
- Title: Post-incident report: <incident-short-id>
- Impact window: start -> end (UTC)
- Summary: High-level chronology and impact table by region and plan.
- Root cause: short summary.
- Mitigation steps taken: list.
- Action items and owner: 1) Improve autoscaler metrics - owner: infra-team - ETA: 30d; 2) Add preflight model evaluation to rollout pipeline - owner: applied-ml - ETA: 14d.

Internal bridge posting checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Bridge opened by IL; record start time and incident short-id.
2. Post initial one-line and severity.
3. Assign ME/MO/CL and confirm on-bridge presence.
4. Capture top-3 hypotheses.
5. Confirm monitoring dashboards and log links.
6. Publish initial public status using Template A.

Handoff and next-shift script
- Handoff timebox: 10 minutes.
- Outgoing oncall must provide:
  - incident short-id and start time
  - current status and last mitigation action
  - immediate next steps and blockers
  - contact list for escalation
- Incoming oncall confirms receipt by reading back the two most important open action items.

Postmortem skeleton (to be used within 72 hours)
- Title: Postmortem: <incident-short-id>
- Summary: 2–3 sentence impact plus customer count.
- Timeline: table of events (time, actor, event).
- Root cause analysis: technical cause and contributing factors.
- Corrective actions: Owner, severity, ETA.
- Learnings and follow-ups: process or monitoring changes.

Game-day syllabus (validates scripts and team readiness)
- Frequency: quarterly (core infra), biannual (model rollouts)
- Duration: 2–3 hours, with a 30-minute hot-debrief.
- Scenarios (pick 2 per run):
  - Fast p99 latency regression in one region with capacity replenishment delay.
  - Silent model-quality drift that affects only a high-value enterprise customer.
  - Autoscaler misconfiguration causing noisy neighbor CPU starvation.
- Success criteria: scripts completed in target timeboxes; public status drafted and approved within 15 minutes; handoff executed without dropped context.

Templates and implementation notes
- Save all comm drafts in #incident-drafts channel and tag @ops-comms for approval.
- Store pinned evidence (metric snapshots, sample traces) in the incident workspace with clear filenames: <incident-id>_p99.png, <incident-id>_trace.json.
- All rollbacks require a ticket in the change system (change-id) and must be referenced in the postmortem.

Appendix: quick reference checklist (single-page)
- If p99 > alert threshold -> open bridge -> post Template A.
- If model rollout in last 60 min -> pin previous version.
- If GPU pool >90% -> enable reserved burst or route traffic out of region.
- If customer-facing errors reported by Support -> tag SL and escalate to IL.

Example Slack status post (copy/paste)
- "[INC-<id>] Investigating increased latency in us-west-2. IL: @oncall-eng. Mitigation: scaling additional replicas. Next update in 15m."

Ownership and governance
- Document owner: Engineering SRE (oncall-and-incident-response). Review cadence: annually or after any Sev1.
- Training: New oncall rotates must complete an incident walkthrough with a senior responder and pass one mock game-day.

Related resources
- Link to monitoring dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/runtime
- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks
- Model rollout checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/rollout-checklist
